title: Testing Simultaneous Conditional Benefit and Harm from Independent Efficacy and Safety Panels
banked_reason: Sound supporting results leave the sharp finite-branch full-class frontier, its attaining full-null test, and matching converse explicitly to-prove; independent validity gate confirms no bounded new repair.
gap_reasons: The headline sharp finite-branch full-class frontier, its attaining full-null test, and matching converse remain explicitly to-prove; the delivered envelope, scalar-face reduction, and mask subexperiment are weaker supporting results rather than the promised target.
As a Stat flagship, the current core does not yet establish its stated rate/optimality frontier: it leaves unmatched logarithms and the possible unequal-budget two-channel branch unresolved.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived finite-sample Bernoulli bounds, scalar-face obstructions, two-record saturation, consistency, and a matched public-amplitude mask subexperiment; the math referee passed them. The exact full-class logarithms, unequal-budget branches, attaining full-null test, and matching converse remain open. Two independent terminal consultations found no new bounded repair, so the field-floor run stops at incremental tier before Lean formalization.
tldr: Treatment may improve a desirable endpoint and increase adverse events in the same covariate region. Independent efficacy and safety panels identify the two conditional mean effects, but estimation noise can create apparent overlap. The directional evidence functional \(Q(P)\) measures covariate-mass-weighted simultaneous positive conditional mean benefit and harm, rather than an individual-effect conjunction. The focal object is the sharp finite-sample separation for this positive-product energy against a null whose nonpositive endpoint may change at every covariate value. The required result is a total original-record test and a matching all-test converse, with explicit logarithms, saturation and unequal-budget branches. The exact finite-branch frontier and any additional two-channel branch are the falsifiable Stage-0 open obligation; the supporting envelope leaves a logarithmic lower/upper gap. Baseline calibration, scalar faces and legal activation masks provide supporting obligations rather than a substitute for that result.
gap: Cai--Tan \cite{CaiTan2015SimultaneousSignals}, Section 3, equations (30)--(31) and Theorem 5, treats sparse prescribed-magnitude Gaussian support-overlap testing. Ma--Cai--Li (2022) \cite{MaCaiLi2022AbsoluteInnerProduct}, Section 2, Theorems 1--2, treats absolute-inner-product estimation and leaves T-score testing and confidence intervals to future work in Section 5. Juditsky--Nemirovski \cite{JuditskyNemirovski2002Positivity}, Theorem 1, gives scalar shape-testing brackets up to logarithms and is a methodological comparator for the fixed-positive face. None supplies the full directional conjunction frontier; the inherited bounded searches located no closer exact theorem.
fill: The sharp-frontier question couples null-supported Bernoulli likelihood comparisons to a continuum-valid multiscale upper procedure. It requires evaluated finite branches and an explicit comparison with the fixed-positive scalar faces under the unchanged benchmark class.
